source.title: Towards the Spectral bias Alleviation by Normalizations in Coordinate Networks
source.authors: Zhicheng Cai; Hao Zhu; Qiu Shen; Xin-Ran Wang; Xun Cao

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper; no material cutoff or garbling is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures training convergence in coordinate networks with and without normalization, bearing on V6's training-speed claim, but uses image-representation tasks and PSNR rather than the version's listed classification settings.
record.gate_note: Only the training-PSNR curves and the paper's explicit description of convergence speed bear on a claim version. Reconstruction metrics, NTK analyses, and results for other methods are not rows because they do not measure the version's stated training-speed outcome.
record.test_reason: The study reports faster training convergence with batch normalization in a new setting: coordinate MLPs fitting images, measured by training PSNR rather than classification accuracy. It is not an original source for V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that normalization reshapes NTK eigenvalue distributions, alleviates spectral bias, accelerates high-frequency convergence, and improves performance across representation and inverse-problem tasks; they also introduce global and cross normalization.
record.recipe_differences: Normalization is added to coordinate networks and assessed on signal-representation training curves; this is not the classification setup in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported speed result is for coordinate networks on Kodak image compression, with separate ReLU and positional-encoding-based methods.

fits_no_version.finding: Layer, global, and cross normalization improve convergence and representation quality; normalization also changes NTK eigenvalue distributions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Several normalization methods alleviate spectral bias in coordinate MLPs by accelerating high-frequency fitting.

record.problems: The training-speed result is presented as a plot without numerical values or uncertainty estimates; the text does not specify the curve's network configuration.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported results measure training speed as stated in V6. Reconstruction-quality metrics and NTK eigenvalue results are outside that version's outcome.

untested.parts: Training classification error in large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels and size or regularization effects.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth degradation, identity shortcuts, and special initialization for deep plain or normalization-free residual networks.
Effects of initialization choices on learning speed, signal propagation, and trainable depth.
Recovery or divergence relative to a measured stability threshold, and sharpness dynamics during training.
Classification settings in the version; maximum tolerable learning rates established by controlled sweeps; convergence at matched learning rates; Fixup and residual networks.

missing.what: Frequency-specific approximation-error trajectories for BN versus unnormalized MLP, PEMLP-1, and PEMLP-5. These directly measure training dynamics and are omitted despite rows_left_out asserting that no other speed results exist. The text reports earlier high-frequency convergence with normalization, especially CN, but does not provide BN-specific numerical trajectories.

record.verdict_notes: The learning-rate difference limits causal attribution, but is not evidence that V6 fails. No limits_scope or challenges verdict is warranted from that confound alone. Figure values were not visually available in the supplied text; observed states rely on the explicit convergence statement.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size, and training duration.
Teacher-student ReLU networks, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Depth effects in plain versus residual convolutional networks; special initialization and normalization-free residual training.
Comparisons of initialization schemes, signal or gradient propagation, and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to stability limits, curvature or sharpness, and divergence.
Tolerance of higher learning rates is not directly compared at matched learning rates; Fixup and residual networks are not tested.
